effect: mean lag 18 weeks vs 22 in the chain

decision: Logitech's customer shares are one row per 10-K, usable from its filing date; graph_asof(date) only sees filed 10-Ks

reason: The graph supplies the structure; the data supply one number

decision: Keep the graph for structure, attribution by route and scenarios; do not claim forecasting gain

decision: Grade every edge's share and lag separately A-D (A audited filing measuring the edge; B filing floor or disclosure plus estimate; C proxy / verbal / one snapshot; D assumption), and mark a D as not_public or not_collected; an edge is as reliable as the weaker of the two, a path as its weakest edge

Nordic lags US electronics-store sales by 18-20 weeks and WSTS billings by 26 weeks; paired differences to the sell-in driver's tau include 0 (+1, -3 weeks): the ~2-quarter peak is consistent with the cycle's timing at Nordic, not the Logitech -> Nordic order lag. decision: Test each relationship for a break rather than list events: Chow (predictive when a segment is shorter than the parameters) and a HAC Wald test at the hand-set regime edges and at the data-dated cycle transitions for Nordic consumer on Logitech sell-through (t-2); stability ranges for 10-K shares and the lag kernel; Wilson intervals for the FCC socket share; the step-2 share path, the 2023 top-10 vs broad split and the bullwhip intervals

Changed: Logitech+GN share of Nordic 14.7% -> 21.5% -> 16.8%; route split in 2023 (top-10 -3%, broad -46%); the Nordic-Logitech link breaks at the end of the shortage (data-dated 2022Q4, Chow p 0.04, 3 obs before) and not at the hand-set 2022Q3 / 2024Q2 edges (p 0.66 / 0.77). Not distinguishable: socket share rise, bullwhip ratio by regime

decision: Separate a SHOCK (dated change in flow, every edge unchanged: propagate it through the graph) from a BREAK (an edge's lag, share or amplitude, or a node's reporting basis changes: condition, exclude, split or restate). Classify every entry of config structural_breaks and regimes once (config/structural_breaks_chain.csv: element changed, buffer, handling, ids) and compute its consequence for Nordic from data in the repo. Work the 2026 Logitech supplier incident as the event study: lost sales -> customers (10-K shares) -> builds (build->sale lag per path, E05 / E08) -> Nordic shipments (rest of the path lead x step-2 content), continuous in weeks and summed into quarters by overlap; chips shipped before the incident or inside the frozen window stay at the holder and are used first at restart; Q3 cuts are push-outs / cancellations of booked orders; share_in_nordic_guide nets the guided quarter

A single shift maps part of a dated shock before its own date (P97)

Conservation: -8.0m = 3.63% x -220m. No forecast changed (step 7c owns the term)

decision: Demand shocks: forward through the order-signal lag (kernel convolution over past demand). Dated supply / event shocks: forward from the event date with causality truncation and conservation (event study, G23). Anticipated demand (seasonal builds, a brand's own guide) moves Nordic ahead of sales; YoY growth removes seasonality, so the kernel's reaction direction is kept

reason: A backward lead shift of a supply shock books losses before the event (P97); the lag was right, the model form was not
evidence: audit table in the reply of 2026-09-27; tests/test_step5.py::test_propagate_is_causal

topic: order-signal lag = physical dwell + information delay (reasoning before computing)
decision: Each edge's lag gets a second, separate term: the information delay of the planning decision the BUYER on that edge makes (the dst node places the order on the src node). Textbook periodic-review order-up-to with an exponentially smoothed forecast: a demand change waits on average half a review period R/2 before the next order, and the smoothed forecast carries it with mean age (1 - alpha) / alpha periods (Brown 1959; Silver, Pyke & Peterson ch. 4), so delay per planning tier = R/2 + (1 - alpha)/alpha x R weeks. Planning tiers: weekly replenishment (Amazon, other retail, resellers, Ingram / TD Synnex ordering from the brand: E11-E22 except the sell-out identities), the brand's monthly S&OP (Logitech / GN ordering builds from the ODM: E08, E10), ODM / EMS MRP (component call-offs: E02, E04, E06, E07), Logitech's own plant = S&OP + MRP (E03, E05: the same two decisions the ODM route crosses, so both routes carry them once), Nordic's distributors' monthly reorder (E01). Sell-out edges (E23, E24) carry no order decision (sell-out is the demand); E25 has no lag. Parameters in config/model.yaml supply_graph.info_delay; which edge carries which planner in config/supply_graph.csv info_delay_planner / info_delay_evidence. All grade D (not public: no company discloses its planning cadence or smoothing), so each planner's range gets the D half-width (+/-100% of the mid) and is not capped by inventory cover (it holds no stock). The Little's-law cap stays on the physical part only; the physical columns are unchanged.
alternatives_considered: (a) keep the physical dwell as the lag (P86: order signals add delays that hold no stock, so it is too short for 'how long until Nordic's revenue moves'); (b) raise the physical lags to the correlation peak (puts the common cycle into the chain, P86); (c) one global lag add-on (hides which tier plans and cannot be checked tier by tier); (d) per-edge independent info-delay draws in the Monte Carlo (one planner, e.g. Logitech's S&OP, sits on several edges: drawn once per planner so it moves them together)
reason: The brief asks how long a change in end demand takes to reach Nordic's revenue: that is an order-signal lag, not the time a unit sits in stock. The information delay is the textbook piece the physical graph leaves out. Values are industry practice, grade D, stated as ranges; the data cannot place them (one down-up cycle, flat correlation surface, P86), so the data are a consistency check (step 4 reasoned 22 wk; near-optimal set 19.5-37 wk), not a fit. Caveat (P100): the additive form assumes a buyer works its buffer down before reordering; the legacy rationale for E08 and step 4's lag_weeks already names S&OP, so part of the planning delay may be counted twice - shown as a sensitivity (smoothing only, R/2 dropped).
effect: Lag answer (signal basis, mid): flow-weighted 19.0 -> 26.5 wk (MC 90% 22.7-29.9; physical 16.3-21.0), Amazon direct 17.3 -> 24.1 wk (20.8-27.3), via Ingram / TD Synnex 20.5 -> 28.7 wk (24.5-32.5); smoothing-only variant 21.6 wk (P100). Upstream Nordic -> brand 14.3 -> 19.6 wk: now inside the sell-in driver's near-optimal set (19.5-37); total 26.5 inside step 4's reasoned 15-32 (mid 22), still below the sell-out proxy's set (32.5-47.5). Step 4 priors move (Logitech edge 1 4.6 -> 7.0 wk, edge 2 14.3 -> 19.6 wk); posterior rule unchanged (data uninformative: posterior = prior). Biggest single input: Logitech / GN S&OP delay (swing 6.5 wk, grade D). DEFAULT: forecasting kernel kept PHYSICAL (supply_graph.lag_basis), measured in a sandbox copy with lag_basis = signal (2026-09-27): kernel mean 1.46 -> 2.04 q; step 6 GR h=1 RMSE 21.05 -> 20.34m (still 3.9x the guide), GR h=2 28.03 -> 28.10m (0.59 -> 0.60x GB), GRg h=2 28.44 -> 28.13m; Nordic Q4 2026 GR point 222.4 -> 221.8m (band 186.5-258.4 -> 185.4-258.1), GRg 216.3 -> 221.2m (+5.0), GRg lag low / high 211.5 / 219.7 -> 211.5 / 212.8; step 7c Nordic Q3 CH 224.5 -> 224.0 (weight 0: final Q3 forecast unchanged), Q4 CH / GR 213.1 / 223.3 -> 213.0 / 222.6; step 6c graph challenger: composite RMSE 3.38 -> 3.51 pts, OLS 2.96 -> 4.80, ridge 2.60 -> 3.66, and its pre-registered live forecast 238.6 -> 237.1m logged under the same spec hash (P101). GR moves trivially, GRg and the pre-registered challenger do not -> the switch is left to the lead (config), the signal basis answers the lag question. Event study (5d) stays physical (a supply shock moves goods already in the pipe; order cuts are modelled there by frozen window / lead time).

topic: route-level demand through the graph (step 5e): Logitech's sell-through allocated across its 10-K routes (reasoning before any score)
decision: Route demand D_r = Logitech sell-through YoY (sell-in YoY + disclosed gap: the total of step 6 GR / step 7c CH) + shrink x sd(total) x (z_r - sum_r w_r z_r); z = each route proxy standardised with its own mean and sd over the quarters known at the origin (>= min_obs quarters, else the route takes the total, as it does in a quarter with no proxy); w_r = the graph's route masses at step 6's origin date (= Logitech 10-K shares Amazon / Ingram / TD Synnex / residual filed by then). Proxies: Amazon total revenue YoY (XBRL); Ingram client & endpoint, else total sales; TD Synnex Endpoint billings; other retail = mean of Best Buy Computing & Mobile comps, CDW revenue, US electronics-store sales. Distributor dollars from 2026Q1 minus structural_breaks.distributor_asp_inflation_2026. Each route is propagated with its own kernel (paths through that Logitech customer; lag basis from config); GN stays on the aggregate path. Then CH's formula (s_t step 2, m step 3). Shrink fixed at 1 before scoring; 0 (= CH-aggregate), 0.5, 'demean' and the other lag basis are reported, never selected. Config route_propagation.
alternatives_considered: (a) Route proxies' LEVELS as route demand (the all-vendor proxies replace Logitech's number): rejected - Amazon includes AWS and ads, distributors memory / servers and 2026 ASP inflation, CDW is B2B IT; all carry the common cycle; Logitech's own sell-through is the one number about Logitech. (b) Raw YoY deviations: Amazon's structural ~10-13% growth becomes a permanent route premium; kept as the 'demean' sensitivity. (c) Route-specific content or multipliers: no evidence Nordic content differs by route. (d) GN by route: GN discloses only annual-report caps.
reason: Prior stated before scoring: with sum_r w_r D_r = total pinned, the split moves CH only through differences between route kernels, sum_r M_r sum_k (K_r,k - K_k) dev_r(t-k). Route lags differ by ~3 weeks (Amazon 17, Ingram / TD Synnex 20 on the physical basis) and all sit on lags 1-2, so at h=1 the split only re-weights t-1 vs t-2 and at h=2 (every lag below h reads t-2) it cannot change anything. Any gain would need mix divergence timed differently by route. Expected small.
effect: As the prior said. h=1: CH-route RMSE 12.74m vs CH-aggregate 12.73m vs GB 7.43m (14 quarters); route increment over CH-aggregate t -0.3; largest gap 0.29m. h=2: identical to CH-aggregate on every quarter (38.4m vs GB 44.1m). Signal-lag basis: gaps <= 0.21m, t -0.7 / +0.1. Live: Q3 2026 CH-route = CH-aggregate 224.5m (routes re-allocate: TD Synnex +1.4 pts, Ingram -1.4, other retail -0.5, Amazon +0.5), Q4 213.1m. Not offered to step 7c as a change: route detail cannot reach the forecast through lags this close; it is shown as structure (who carries the demand) only.

topic: route proxies as a nowcast of Logitech's unreported quarter (step 5f; reasoning and adoption rule before any score)
decision: At the h=2 origin of Nordic t (day before Nordic reports t-1 = t-1 end + 21 d) Logitech has not reported t-1. Nowcast y(t-1) = Logitech sell-through YoY (sell-in YoY + gap) from proxies released by then (release date = stored filing date or period end + a graded typical lag, config route_nowcast.release_lag): TD Synnex revenue (FQ Jun-Aug: 2 of 3 months), Endpoint billings (no live value), Best Buy Computing & Mobile comps (May-Jul: 1 month), US electronics-store sales months 1-2 (partial-quarter YoY). Amazon, Ingram, CDW report after Nordic: excluded by the rule. Models: N0 persistence (default); N1 Logitech's guide (comparison only); N2 y(q) = y(q-1) + b x mean_j dx_j/sd_j (one slope through the origin, expanding window from 2021Q4, b = 0 below 6 pairs; N2c composite, N2s TD Synnex revenue, N2e Endpoint). Each fed to step 6 GR (forecast_row) and step 7c CH through the graph kernel, with a one-entry ahead map (t-1 only). Adoption rule set by the analyst on 2026-09-27: default = persistence (a modelling assumption); a proxy nowcast replaces it only if its RMSE is below N0's on the same quarters AND DM t <= -2 or encompassing t >= 2, AND Nordic h=2 GR is not worse; Logitech's guide is not a candidate (the analyst considers it known to be inaccurate) and is never pre-registered.
alternatives_considered: (a) Level bridge y = a + b x (the textbook bridge equation): rejected - all-vendor levels (TD Synnex +38% in 2026 on memory) would become Logitech's level; the change form nests persistence (b = 0). (b) Several regressors / a factor model: ~13 training pairs, one slope only. (c) N3 = guide + proxy adjustment: needs the guide (user rule) and has 5 observations. (d) Aligning proxies by the quarter they describe: look-ahead (P105). (e) Distributors' own guides (Ingram's Q3 guide is out 30 Jul): a forecast, all-vendor, not pre-declared; left out. (f) First-release vintages of retail sales (ALFRED): a new data source; revision risk disclosed (P108).
reason: Prior before scoring: modest at best - proxies are all-vendor / all-category and carry the common cycle, Logitech is ~0.8% of TD Synnex's revenue, two of three overlap the target by 1-2 months, TD Synnex's 2026 dollars are memory ASPs, and Logitech's YoY is persistent. The analyst's rule puts the burden of proof on the proxies because persistence is transparent and a wrong nowcast moves Nordic's Q4 line; the guide is excluded on its record (step 7e / F24).
evidence: steps/step5_supply_graph/outputs/route_nowcast.md; route_nowcast.csv; route_nowcast_nordic.csv; route_nowcast_scores.csv; route_nowcast_availability.csv; route_nowcast_prereg_log.csv; tests/test_route_nowcast.py
effect: As the prior said: no proxy nowcast beats persistence. Nowcast RMSE vs N0 on the same quarters: N2c 5.60 vs 4.96 pts (n 13, DM t +0.5), N2s 4.49 vs 4.22 (n 8, +0.7), N2e 4.25 vs 4.22 (n 8, +0.1); guide (comparison) 4.04 vs 2.93 (n 5). Nordic h=2 GR: persistence 28.0m (n 9), N2c 27.4 (DM t -2.5 but 95% of the gain from 3 quarters and the nowcast itself worse: P109), N2s 28.5, N2e 27.7, guide 28.4; CH 38.4 for every variant. Verdict: persistence (N0) stays the default; nothing changes in step 7. Live (pre-registered): Logitech 2026Q3 sell-through YoY N0 10.9, N2c 12.7, N2s 11.8 (guide 5.4, not registered); Nordic 2026Q4 GR 223.3 / 223.9 / 223.8m, CH 213.1 / 213.4 / 213.2m. Check on 27 Oct when Logitech reports. Replication: N0 / N1 graph demand = step 6 GR / GRg exactly.

topic: events of 2021-26 tested one by one (step 5c)
decision: Answer the brief's structural-break question by event: each event at a date fixed in config, typed as relationship break, input moved, shock, proxy break or forward risk, with a test where the data allow. Added: 2025 US tariffs (price step from the quoted +150 bp gross-margin lift = 2.75% of sales; unit driver = dollar driver minus the step; Chow across the step; purchase pull-in as a timing shock), post-COVID normalisation (decomposition of Nordic's 2022-24 consumer fall into the Logitech+GN slice and the rest), AI / memory cycle (WSTS vs Nordic: Fisher z and Chow; distributor minus Logitech gap: Welch t), Nordic capacity (forward risk)
alternatives_considered: Keep the event list by tool (G22 / 5d); use the unsourced '~10% US list price' from the research notes; call the AI / memory decoupling a break on the levels alone
reason: Analyst review 2026-09-27: section 4 answered by tool and mixed breaks, shocks and reporting items; three candidate events were not assessed
effect: Tariffs: $-vs-units break of up to 2.75 pts in the Logitech driver (2025Q2-2026Q1); link across it not distinguishable (Chow p 0.78 / 0.91, 3 quarters after); live effect on Nordic's chain term ~0.5m (weight 0: forecast unchanged). Normalisation: 2023 Nordic consumer -38%, of which the Logitech+GN slice -3 pts and the rest -34 pts; link stable at 2024Q2 (p 0.77): input moved, relationship stable. AI / memory: visible in levels (WSTS +129% vs Nordic +33%; TD Synnex-Logitech gap +4, +11, +24) but not significant on this sample (Fisher-z p 0.28, Chow p 0.57; Welch p 0.15); both series context only. Microchip MCU distributor days unaffected (28, 26, 25). Capacity: risk, watched (W4)

topic: industry-cycle regression as a pre-registered Q4 challenger (step 5g; reasoning, spec and adoption bar before any score)
decision: CYC: Nordic consumer YoY at t (GR's target; total = guide-anchored benchmark + consumer tilt, as GR) on ONE industry-cycle series at t-2, OLS, expanding window, through step 6's forecast_row at h=2 (same targets, training rows, supply-constrained rule (config backtest: kept, as GR), guide rows, GB). Series: US electronics-store sales YoY (RSEAS, Census via FRED, grade A). Point in time: a cycle quarter is published when its third month is (quarter end + release lag: RSEAS 45 d = route_nowcast.release_lag.rseas; WSTS 45 d, grade C); origin(t) = the day before Nordic reports t-1; t-2 is the last full quarter out by then, t-1 is filled by persistence (F24), no partial quarters. Pre-stated robustness: CYCw (WSTS world billings YoY at t-2 instead) and CYCg (RSEAS + GR's graph demand, two slopes: the cycle beyond Logitech). Bar (config cycle_challenger.adoption, before scoring): on the quarters where CYC, GR, CH, GB and the actual all exist, RMSE < GR's AND (DM-HLN t <= -2 OR encompassing t >= 2 over GR) AND top-3 share of the squared-error gain < 0.5. Met or not, CYC is a pre-registered challenger for Q4 2026 only (steps/step5_supply_graph/outputs/cycle_challenger_prereg_log.csv); F22 / F24 stay; adoption for later prints is the analyst's call. (GR + CYC) / 2 scored as a diagnostic only.
alternatives_considered: (a) WSTS as primary (G21: Nordic lags it by ~26 weeks = lag 2): rejected before scoring - world billings are dominated by AI logic and memory prices from 2024 (G28, P110: WSTS +129% YoY in 2026Q2 vs Nordic +33%); the live input (2026Q2, +129%) is 3.4x the largest value in its training rows (+38%), so the slope would be extrapolated; kept as robustness CYCw to show it. WSTS has no product split in the repo (region split only in the uncached workbook). (b) TD Synnex / Ingram sales: all-vendor IT distribution, memory ASPs in 2026, merger mask 2021Q4-2022Q3, Logitech <1% of them: rejected. (c) Microchip distributor days (step 3): a channel-inventory state, already in the 6c composite and in the anchor's building state (F20) - reusing it re-opens the stopped factor search (B40) and double counts the anchor: rejected. (d) Two cycle series or a factor model: n 9-18 training rows, one cycle (P58): one slope. (e) Partial-quarter RSEAS for t-1 (months 1-2 are out at the origin): the bridge lost to persistence in step 5f (G27); t-1 by persistence. (f) Excluding the supply-constrained rows (2022Q1-Q2, whose regressors carry the 2020 lockdown base): would change the training rule relative to GR; reported as step 6's own sensitivity flip for both models, not selected.
reason: P77: GR's slope is ~3x the attribution slice because Nordic's other consumer customers ride the same cycle; the question is whether an industry series times that cycle better than Logitech through the graph. Consumer end demand is the hypothesised common driver of Nordic's consumer segment; the inventory amplification (Nordic -38% in 2023 against RSEAS -5%) is left to the slope, as in GR. One slope, the same target, window and origin make CYC a pure swap of GR's regressor, so the scores compare information, not specification. Analyst approval 2026-09-27 lifts Pipeline B's 'context only, never a regressor' rule for this challenger only; the forecast does not read it. Prior before scoring: weak - RSEAS is US-only, nominal (2025 tariff pass-through), includes appliances and moves +-5% outside COVID; Logitech's own sell-through is the closer measure of the same end demand.
effect: As the prior said, the bar is not met. On the 9 quarters where CYC, GR, CH and GB all exist (2024Q2-2026Q2, h=2): RMSE CYC 38.8m, GR 28.0, CH 39.4, GB 47.2; CYC bias -30.7m, closer than GR in 2 of 9 quarters; DM-HLN t +1.6 (worse); encompassing CYC over GR beta +2.94 (t +2.3; drop one quarter: 1.5 without 2025Q2, P114), GR over CYC beta -1.94 (t -1.5); no net squared-error gain (top-3 share n/a). Robustness: WSTS 25.9m (0.92x GR, DM t -1.0) but live input +129% = 3.4x its scored range -> Q4 379m (P113); RSEAS + graph demand 36.7m. (GR + CYC) / 2: 31.5m (diagnostic). Step 6 sensitivity (supply-constrained out, n 7): CYC 36.0 vs GR 34.5. Live Nordic 2026Q4 (incident -0.9m in every line): GR 222.4, CH 212.2, CYC 208.3 (158.6-258.0, 1.28 x 38.8), GB 221.1; beyond the Logitech / GN slice GR sees +10.2m of cycle, CYC -3.9m. Pre-registered in cycle_challenger_prereg_log.csv; check 2027-02-05. Q4 forecast unchanged (GR, F22 / F24).

topic: CYC decomposition against the new point model GRi

reason: Analyst request 2026-09-27 after GRi (F26, forecast fill) replaced GR: does GRi fit the industry reading better? Levels carry each model's bias (CYC -30.7m walk-forward bias), so only anomalies compare readings
